summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with worsening left calf pain and nighttime respiratory symptoms following recent travel. Imaging confirmed a deep vein thrombosis in the left posterior tibial veins, and a CT angiogram revealed acute pulmonary emboli in the right upper, middle, and lower pulmonary arteries. She remained hemodynamically stable without need for thrombolysis. Anticoagulation with Lovenox was initiated, leading to clinical improvement in respiratory symptoms and ambulatory tolerance. Chronic issues including graft-versus-host disease affecting the eyes, skin, and mouth were managed with ongoing prednisone and eye medications. The patient was discharged home on Lovenox with plans for long-term anticoagulation and follow-up with her oncologist.
problems: Acute venous embolism and thrombosis of deep vessels of distal lower extremity
